one_liner: Safe no_std Rust QOI encoder/decoder; decodes about 6% faster than the qoi crate but encodes about 14% slower.
what_it_does: A pure-Rust (forbid(unsafe_code), no_std with optional alloc) encoder and decoder for the QOI lossless image format, 8-bit RGB or RGBA only. The API is a small `Qoi { width, height, colors }` descriptor with `encode`/`encode_alloc` and `decode`/`decode_alloc`/`decode_header` over caller-supplied byte slices, plus `encode_range`/`decode_range` entry points that carry index, previous pixel and run state between calls for row-by-row streaming. It decodes into the channel count stored in the header only (no RGB-to-RGBA conversion option), and the declared `io` feature has no code behind it, so there is no std::io reader/writer API.
how_it_is_fast: The decoder is a single loop that pattern-matches slice heads on the opcode byte ranges (INDEX, DIFF, LUMA, RGB, RGBA, RUN) and fills runs with `slice::fill` instead of per-pixel writes, with no per-byte bounds checks beyond the slice patterns. The colour-index hash (r*3+g*5+b*7+a*11 mod 64) is computed with one 64-bit multiply over a masked, duplicated pixel word (the 'hardqoi' bit hack merged in January 2026, which saves an AND; I checked it against the spec formula on 200,000 random pixels with no mismatch). The encoder replaces a run of exactly one with a QOI_OP_INDEX to the previous pixel (same size, slightly cheaper to decode), and the decoder skips the index write after INDEX and RUN chunks that qoi.h performs on every chunk.
when_to_use: Rust projects, including no_std or embedded targets, that need a tiny dependency-free QOI codec with no unsafe code.

Decode-heavy workloads (asset loading of QOI files you produced yourself), where the only same-run measurement shows it about 6% faster than the qoi crate on an Apple M1 and faster in 12 of 13 suite directories.
Row-by-row or tiled decode into a fixed buffer via `decode_range`, now that the June 2026 fix (PR #14) carries a QOI_OP_RUN across call boundaries instead of panicking.
Builds where compile time matters: the crate is three source files with no dependencies since 0.6.3.
when_not_to_use: C++ projects: it is a Rust crate with no C API; use qoi.h or qoixx instead.
Encode-heavy workloads: in the same-run M1 benchmark the qoi crate encodes about 14% faster overall and faster in all 13 directories.

Decoding QOI files from arbitrary third-party encoders where spec conformance matters: the decoder does not add the pixel to the colour index after QOI_OP_RUN (open issue #11 from the QOI author, linked to phoboslab/qoi#258 and its edgecase.qoi), so a stream that starts with a run and later indexes slot 53 decodes as transparent instead of opaque black.

Projects pinned to a Rust toolchain older than 1.88: 0.6.3 uses `slice::as_chunks`/`as_chunks_mut` (stabilised in Rust 1.88.0, 2025-06-26) after the bytemuck removal, but Cargo.toml declares no rust-version, so a `^0.6` requirement breaks on update for older compilers.
Anything needing std::io streaming, channel conversion on decode, more than 8 bits per channel, or better compression than PNG.

integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.88 for 0.6.3 (uses slice::as_chunks; not declared in Cargo.toml); edition 2018
integration.platforms: any (portable scalar Rust; no SIMD; the hash constant goes through to_le() so it is endian-correct)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; the functions keep no global state and work only on caller-supplied buffers and state
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: it reads and writes the same QOI format as qoi.h and the qoi crate (same output sizes in the bench), but its API differs and its decoder diverges from the spec on the leading-QOI_OP_RUN edge case

gotchas: Correctness bug in the release most users have: crates.io 0.6.1 (2022-02-18, 4,520,345 of the crate's roughly 4.54 million downloads) encodes 3-channel RGB images incorrectly. Its RGB encoder kept a 3-byte colour index zero-filled at start, so the first pure-black pixel matched an empty slot and was written as QOI_OP_INDEX, which a spec decoder reads as transparent black; that is my reading of the f4f1537 diff. Issue #6 (2022-02-20, still open, no maintainer reply) lists over 140 suite images where reference decoding of rapid-qoi output differs. The fix (f4f1537, 'Use 4 channel index for all cases', 2022-05-28, version 0.6.2) was never published; it first reached crates.io in 0.6.3 on 2026-08-26. The benchmark converts every image to RGBA with to_rgba8, so the published timings exercise the unaffected 4-channel path.

The 3-channel decoder discards the alpha byte of QOI_OP_RGBA chunks and hashes pixels with alpha 255, while qoi.h keeps alpha internally whatever channel count is requested. A 3-channel file containing RGBA chunks with alpha below 255 could therefore resolve later QOI_OP_INDEX chunks differently. This comes from reading the source and was not tested.

Testing is thin. The only test is tests/run_at_edge.rs (the #13 regression), and CI runs `cargo test` only. validate.sh, a round-trip check against the reference qoiconv, covers only the screenshot_game directory and is not wired into CI. The crate has no fuzzing, unlike the qoi crate, which is round-trip-tested against the C reference and fuzz-tested.
The `io` feature in Cargo.toml has no code behind it, and decode always outputs the header's channel count.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over qoi (qoi-rust) only when decode speed matters more than encode speed and you control the encoder, or want the smallest dependency-free no_std crate; qoi-rust encodes faster in the same run, offers std::io streaming, declares MSRV 1.62, and is fuzz- and round-trip-tested. For C or C++ callers, qoixx or the reference qoi.h (or qoi-asm on x86-64-v3) are the relevant siblings, since rapid-qoi has no C API.
verified_claims_summary: The README headline (decode 1.43x faster on an unnamed Intel i9 and 1.52x on an Apple M1) compares a Rust-harness rapid_qoi run against a separate run of phoboslab's C qoibench.c. On M1 the qoi crate alone in that same Rust harness already decodes 1.44x faster than the C row (1.161 vs 1.676 ms, derived from page data), so most of the headline gap is harness and implementation-language difference, not rapid-qoi-specific. The only same-run comparison (benches/m1/rapid.md, 1 timed run per image, RGBA, qoi_benchmark_suite minus 2 PNGs the image crate rejects) shows decode 1.100 vs 1.161 ms (1.06x) and encode 1.836 vs 1.614 ms (0.88x) against the qoi crate 0.4, with rustc version, flags and the i9 model unstated.
status_note: Lightly maintained: the 2026 commits are contributor PRs (hash bit hack, run-clamp fix) plus a bytemuck removal, and 0.6.3 shipped on 2026-08-26, but correctness issues #6 and #11 have stayed open since 2022-2023 without a reply. The published benchmark files date from December 2021 to February 2022 and predate the September 2022 fix of an inverted `unlikely` branch hint (c5359a5) and the 2026 hash change, so no published number describes 0.6.3. MIT OR Apache-2.0, small enough to vendor.
